To say DXVK came out of no where would be an understatement. It went from the beginning of this year to a "oh, this is an interesting project; will it go anywhere" to something more akin to "who the hell is this guy and how is he able to get all this shit done by himself?".

DXVK has been doing such a great job of translating the DX11 API to Vulkan, that it is now feasible to run many DirectX11 titles through Wine, with little to no issues (at least those caused by the DirectX11 feature set - DRM and general Wine bug will always haunt you). The only main hurdle left to jump is lack of Stream Output, but already this one-man-wonder has hinted that he has something in the works to get around that hurdle as well.

Damn. Anyway, onto the guide.

Installing DXVK (Binary Release) - Arch Linux (Arch Based Distributions)

In order to install DXVK on Arch Linux we'll need to install the package from the AUR (Arch User Repository). This is a User maintained repository containing thousands of additional packages which can be installed on Arch Linux based distributions.

There are two ways to achieve this:

  • Using an AUR Helper tool from the terminal
  • Downloading the PKGBUILD files for the dxvk-bin package, which will provide the 32-bit and 64-bit packages from the AUR, and building the software using makepkg.

Prerequisites

The base-devel group of packages are required to build software from the AUR. Make sure this group is installed by typing:

sudo pacman -S base-devel --needed

Into the terminal, before proceeding, and any missing packages from that group will be installed. It should already be installed, as part of the standard Arch install procedure, but there is no harm in checking.

Install DXVK using AUR Helper (pacaur)

First things first, if pacaur is not already installed, install it by opening the terminal and typing in:

sudo pacman -S pacaur

Once installed, you can use pacaur to install DXVK from the AUR by typing:

pacaur -S dxvk-bin

Install DXVK using AUR PKGBUILD files

From the terminal, change the current directory to the Downloads folder (or another location if you prefer, this is just an example):

cd ~/Downloads

Then obtain the tar ball for the DXVK bin release from the AUR website and extract it.

curl -L -O https://aur.archlinux.org/cgit/aur.git/snapshot/dxvk-bin.tar.gz && tar xvzf dxvk-bin.tar.gz

Change to the newly created folder "dxvk-bin" containing the extracted files:

cd ./dxvk-bin

Lastly, run makepkg as a normal user (not using sudo) to build and install the dxvk software packages:

makepkg -si

Installing DXVK (Binary Release) - Ubuntu Linux (Ubuntu Based Distributions) & Solus Linux

Unfortunately I could not locate any packages for installing DXVK on Ubuntu or Solus, so we'll have to do it the manual way. If you know of a solution to automate the process, let me know.

Download the latest release from the DXVK GitHub page and extract it.

You can do this with your web browser and file manager, or in the terminal with:

cd ~/Downloads && curl -L -O https://github.com/doitsujin/dxvk/releases/download/v0.64/dxvk-0.64.tar.gz && tar xvzf dxvk-0.64.tar.gz

Copy the extracted folder and contents to a different location, if you prefer, or leave it where it is in ~/Downloads/dxvk-0.64, just remember the path to the folder, as it will be needed in the next step.

Note: This will download the current release of DXVK as of writing this guide. DXVK is developing fast, so new releases are thrown out nearly every month or so. Check here regularly to see if a newer version has been released.

Activating DXVK in a Wineprefix - Arch Linux (Arch Based Distributions)

DXVK replaces the dxgi and d3d11 DLLs used for DirectX11 in Wine, so in order to use DXVK, each Wineprefix you want to use it in, must have one or both of the following commands run against it, depending on if the prefix is 32-bit or 64-bit:

WINEPREFIX=/path/to/your/prefix setup_dxvk32

WINEPREFIX=/path/to/your/prefix setup_dxvk64

This does two things.

  1. It copies the dxgi.dll and d3d11.dll files into the Wineprefixes' system32 (64bit) and syswow64 (32bit on a 64bit Wineprefix) folders.
  2. It changes the Library Override settings displayed in Winecfg for dxgi and d3d11 to Native (Windows).

Note: A 64bit Wineprefix will still require the 32bit DXVK DLLs, as you will most likely be running a 32bit application inside of that prefix.

And that's it, DXVK is ready to use in that Wineprefix the next time you launch a DX11 game. To check if it is working, you can use the environment variable DXVK_HUD=1 to display a HUD while running the game.

Example (Not sure if this syntax is correct, need to check when back at my rig):

export DXVK_HUD=1 && WINEPREFIX=/path/to/your/prefix wine /path/to/your/game/exe.exe

Activating DXVK in a Wineprefix - Ubuntu Linux (Ubuntu Based Distributions) & Solus Linux

As I could not locate a package to install for these two distributions, the steps required to turn on DXVK require a tad more typing into the terminal. To turn DXVK on, you would enter the following:

WINEPREFIX=/path/to/your/prefix bash /path/to/where/you/saved/DXVK_Folder/x32/setup_dxvk.sh

WINEPREFIX=/path/to/your/prefix bash /path/to/where/you/saved/DXVK_Folder/x64/setup_dxvk.sh

This does the same steps as running the setup command from the Arch Linux package. It copies the DLLs into the Wineprefixes' Windows system folders and sets the DLL Overrides to Native (Windows).

As before, to check if it is working, you can use DXVK_HUD=1 from the terminal, to display the DXVK HUD.

export DXVK_HUD=1 && WINEPREFIX=/path/to/your/prefix wine /path/to/your/game/exe.exe

Deactivating DXVK in a Wineprefix

To turn DXVK off and revert to the Builtin Wine DX11 DLLs, you would run the exact same commands as previously, but include reset at the end of the command.

For example:

WINEPREFIX=/path/to/your/prefix setup_dxvk64 reset

or

WINEPREFIX=/path/to/your/prefix bash /path/to/where/you/saved/DXVK_Folder/x32/setup_dxvk.sh reset

Remember to rerun both commands for 32 and 64bit, with the reset switch, to fully revert the Wineprefix to Wined3d.

DXVK HUD - Additional Options

Although not intended as a user-friendly feature (debugging purposes only) the DXVK_HUD has several configuration options that can be applied, which are shown below:

  • devinfo: Displays the name of the GPU and the driver version.
  • fps: Shows the current frame rate.
  • frametimes: Shows a frame time graph.
  • submissions: Shows the number of command buffers submitted per frame.
  • drawcalls: Shows the number of draw calls and render passes per frame.
  • pipelines: Shows the total number of graphics and compute pipelines.
  • memory: Shows the amount of device memory allocated and used.
  • version: Shows DXVK version.

So for example, if you wanted to show the fps, graphs, and DXVK version numbers, you would use:

DXVK_HUD=fps,frametimes,version

DXVK Configuration File

DXVK also stores a configuration file in the current working directory, which can be modified if required. The location of this config file can also be changed.

See this DXVK Wiki page for more information.
